question: Which exact firmware addresses give the UI host MiSans-Medium 24/28 label styles, object flag add/clear and a correct lv_bar_create?
callsite_evidence: sub_C4C065C (lvx_theme_default_init) initialises 0x2010CEE0 with constructor arguments (1, 0x18, 0) and 0x2010CEF8 with (1, 0x1C, 0); the same position in the other 10 Pro firmware holds the 12-byte-stride neighbour objects.

Object flag veneers (LDR.W PC,[PC], literal targets equal in 3.101.036 and 3.101.043): library 0x1C028BD9 = add_flag at 0xc588960 / 0xcac00c0 (the second table is the existing lvx_object_add_flag record), library 0x1C028C85 = clear_flag at 0xc5891b0 / 0xcac0540. Identification: lvx_page_title_create makes the back icon clickable with the 0x1C028BD9 veneer(icon, 2) where Band 11's matches call FW_LV_OBJECT_ADD_FLAG (sub_C38404C), and lvx_page_msgbox set-up calls the 0x1C028C85 veneer with 2 and 16 where Band 11 calls FW_LV_OBJECT_CLEAR_FLAG (sub_C3840D8).
The previous lv_bar_create record (0xc0c21d8) is not a lvgl veneer; the veneer with the same library target 0x1C073859 as 3.101.036 0x0C588320 is at 0xc588b90.

Call-site analysis of the stock UI code (identical in 3.101.036 and 3.101.043; the veneer jumps to the version-stable LVGL library entry 0x1C028D39): bt_item_able_status (3.101.043 sub_C561D98) dims an item and calls the 0x1C028D09 veneer with 0x80 when it is disabled, and calls the 0x1C028D39 veneer with the same 0x80 when it is enabled again; sub_C58FE78 reads the object's state through the 0x1C028DC5 veneer, passes it to the 0x1C028D39 veneer to clear it and then sets 3 or 2 through 0x1C028D09. 0x80 is LV_STATE_DISABLED, so 0x1C028D09 is lv_obj_add_state, 0x1C028D39 is lv_obj_remove_state and 0x1C028DC5 is lv_obj_get_state. The same stock code pairs 0x1C028C85 (clear_flag) with 0x1C028BD9 (add_flag) for the CLICKABLE flag 2. The old name lv_obj_set_hidden was wrong: set_hidden(obj, 1) clears the CHECKED state bit and does not hide anything. LVGL 9 has no set_hidden; hiding is add_flag / clear_flag with LV_OBJ_FLAG_HIDDEN (1), which the UI host uses.
ownership_analysis: Style objects are firmware-owned, borrowed read-only through lvx_style_apply. Flag veneers take a borrowed LVGL object.
unsafe_assumptions: Static recovery only; Mirage results are emulator evidence, not device verification.
recommended_probe: Run the ui-gallery module on a Band 10 Pro and compare label typography, hide/show and bar rendering with Band 11.
